description.value: The study examined neural activation during aversive-face processing in recently detoxified alcohol-dependent patients versus healthy controls and tested associations with lifetime alcohol intake and prospective treatment outcome.

spans.text: In this study, functional brain imaging was used to examine the hypothesis that neural activation elicited by a cue-comparison paradigm presenting aversive faces versus neutral shapes is diminished in ADP compared with healthy control subjects (HC).

value: we hypothesized that neural activation elicited by a cue-comparison paradigm presenting aversive faces versus neutral shapes is diminished in ADP compared with healthy control subjects (HC).

We hypothesized that such a reduced brain response in the contrast ‘faces–shapes’ is especially pronounced in regions that are crucial in emotional face processing, i.e. the amygdala, the FG, and—as suggested by Salloum et al . ( 2007 )—the affective division of the ACC (i.e. rostral ACC).

description.value: Observational, cross-sectional comparison of recently detoxified alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls, with prospective six-month follow-up of treatment outcome in patients.

clinical_characteristics.value: Recently detoxified alcohol-dependent patients; detoxification occurred 4–24 days before MRI. Alcohol dependence severity, craving, lifetime alcohol consumption, anxiety, depression, impulsivity and smoking dependence were assessed.
